scope: Three new web techniques and existing OAuth/OIDC update
user_approval: User explicitly approved resources, procedures and final exact drafts before saving.
validation: Independent critic JSON outputs replayed through production publication_review.assess; no live production model invocation. Saved bytes equal reviewed hashes.
limitations: Offline authoring review only; no target probes or effectiveness rating. Historical library provenance not reconstructed.

review.reason: The complete draft explicitly inventories all identifiable bundle dependencies and distinct versions, preserves evidence locations and conflicting clues, and separates package presence, runtime use, affectedness and impact. Sensitive-content and integrity comparisons have actual audience/trust prerequisites and controls; fixture demonstrations do not imply target compromise. Retained SRI and OWASP references support the described background without claiming the original inventory procedure is source-verified.

The complete draft preserves existing OAuth/OIDC flow tests and supplies a separate discovery/key-fetch branch with issuer provenance, actual fetch-location prerequisites, isolated actor-controlled variations, legitimate cross-host and key-rotation controls, synthetic credential handling, cache isolation and restoration. It distinguishes metadata retrieval from prohibited destinations, leaked credentials and wrong-context token acceptance. Inspected retained OAuth cheat sheet, RFC 9700, OIDC Core and Discovery passages support the attributed facts; original outbound-fetch procedures are honestly distinguished from source-backed requirements. No material issues found.

The complete draft satisfies the agreed full-lifecycle method. Effective security inheritance, overrides, alternatives and anonymous access are distinguished from deployed authorization; audience policy, isolated actor controls, actual protected results and bounded scope prevent disclosure and status-code false positives. Retained OpenAPI and OWASP passages support the stated source contributions.

The complete draft provides actionable channel-specific comparisons with synthetic values, intended-recipient policy, fresh-context and receiver controls, cleanup, and explicit unavailable-evidence limits. It correctly qualifies broad query-string exposure claims using actual referrer behavior and separates confidentiality from credential replay. Retained OWASP, Referrer Policy draft and RFC 9700 passages support the stated background and limitations.
